levels.1: Category 1 (F): an easy ascent, mostly walking and scrambling on simple terrain or a gentle glacier. Good fitness and basic mountain experience are enough, but altitude and weather still matter.
levels.2: Category 2 (PD): some easy climbing (II–III) and snow or ice slopes. Bring a rope for exposed parts and know how to use crampons and an ice axe.
levels.3: Category 3 (AD): sustained climbing with belayed pitches up to III–IV and steeper snow and ice. You need rope work, anchor building and experience from category 2 routes.
levels.4: Category 4 (D): technical rock (IV–V) or ice up to about 60°, long days and possibly a bivouac. For experienced alpine teams.
levels.5: Category 5 (TD): very difficult, sustained V–VI climbing or steep ice, sometimes aid. A multi-day commitment with serious objective danger.
levels.6: Category 6 (ED): extreme routes on the hardest faces and walls. Only for very experienced alpinists.

mountain.emergency_text: 112 is the single emergency number in Georgia (rescue, ambulance, police). Tell someone your route and when you'll be back before you start.
mountain.plan_message_sos: If I don't check in by the return time, call 112.
mountain.emergency_lead: One number for mountain rescue, ambulance, fire and police anywhere in Georgia. The call is free; say "mountain rescue" and that you are on a climbing route.
mountain.emergency_app: Before the trip, install the 112 Georgia app: its SOS button sends your location to the dispatcher.
mountain.say_where_text: the route ({{route}}), the part of it, and your GPS coordinates.
mountain.say_what_text: injuries, how many people need help, weather and how much daylight is left.
mountain.say_phone_text: keep the phone on, save battery and stay where you are if it is safe.
mountain.location_error: Couldn't get your location. Turn on location (GPS) and try again.
mountain.no_signal: No signal? Move to higher, open ground and try again. A text message often gets through when a call doesn't.
mountain.plan_hint: Tell someone where you're going and when you'll be back. If you don't check in, they call 112 with your route.
